name: bm-v3-junction-bending-rigidity
claim: SUPERSEDED by the 2026-10-01 cross-check. This study originally explained the soft modulus as a central-force rigidity-percolation effect (z ≤ 3 < 4). The released code is NOT central-force — it sets junction angles (NC1 180° k=4.0, 7S 155°/60°) — so that explanation does not describe the published model, which carries those angles and is still soft (≈0.03 Pa). What this sweep actually shows: with angles OFF (our earlier transcription) and the corrected params, the network is sub-isostatic (z tops out ≈2.0) and soft — a property of the angle- off transcription, not of the paper.
experiment: Sweep the max crosslinks per end (a bundling proxy: NC1×k + 7S×m, k,m rising) so the mean coordination z climbs, and measure the seed-ensemble elastic modulus vs z against the z = 4 threshold.
result: With the corrected released params and angles off, raising the crosslink caps lifts z only to ~2.0 and the modulus stays consistent with zero at every rung — consistent with a sparse, sub-isostatic angle-off network. But this is NOT the mechanism of the published model's softness: the released model has junction angles and is still soft (≈0.03 Pa), which the spec attributes to missing components, thin-sheet geometry and absent pre-stress, not to sub-isostatic connectivity. The rigidity-percolation framing is retired as the explanation.

purpose.question: Can more crosslink connectivity rigidify the v1 network, or is bending required?
purpose.mechanism: Maxwell rigidity percolation: a central-force network is floppy below z = 2d (= 4 in 2D). Bond-bending constraints lower the threshold and rigidify sub- isostatic networks.
purpose.expected_outcome: Modulus stays ~0 while z < 4; since NC1×1 + 7S×3 caps z at 3, connectivity alone never rigidifies — bending does.

key_assumptions: Mean coordination z = 1 + n_crosslinks/n_rods (beads = 2·n_rods; bonds = intra + crosslinks).
Raising NC1/7S max crosslinks is a proxy for lateral bundling (more junctions).
Same clean-room parameters and force-independent off-rate as stage 1.

findings.explanation: NC1×1 + 7S×3 caps z at 3; bundling raises it but the geometry saturates below 4.

config.title: Rigidity sweep — modulus vs coordination z

limitations: Cross-check (2026-10-01): the released model is NOT central-force — it sets NC1/7S junction angles (bending). The rigidity-percolation premise here is general physics but does not describe the published model, which is angle-stabilized. See references/cross-check-vs-released-code.md.
Clean-room parameters transcribed from the spec; the authors' LAMMPS input scripts are now public (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20719515) and not yet cross-checked against this build.
Bundling is modelled only as raised crosslink caps, not explicit lateral-association bonds.
Junction bending is not yet implemented — this study motivates it, does not test it.
Same LJ-unit / energy-scale caveat as stage 1.

report.title: Stage v3 — rigidity percolation (superseded explanation)
report.verdict: The rigidity-percolation explanation for the soft modulus is retired by the 2026-10-01 cross-check: the released model is not central-force (it has junction angles) and is soft anyway. This sweep documents only that our angle-off transcription is sub-isostatic and soft; it does not explain the published model.
report.main_insight: The published model's softness is not a crosslink-connectivity effect — it persists despite the junction angles, so it must come from the factors the spec names (missing components, thin-sheet geometry, no pre-stress). Connectivity is not the lever.

sources.note: The two-bead-rod + stochastic-crosslink model; its ≈0.03 Pa modulus is the near-floppy regime this study explains.

derived.insight: Raising NC1/7S crosslinks lifts z to only ~3.7 (never 4), and the modulus stays consistent with zero throughout — central-force connectivity cannot rigidify the v1 sheet.
